subject: pygments vs. rouge in GitHub pages? font size control?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: pygments vs. rouge in GitHub pages? font size control?
parts:
It looks like they updated the server and it is no longer
finding pygments (if it ever was).

Also, you can see on this page:

http://mc-stan.org/citations/

that the font mysteriously (to me, at least) changes to a smaller
size in the last few items. If I get rid of the headers in
between, everything's fine. I friggin' hate all this markdown
indirection in between what I want to render and me!

- Bob

> On Feb 3, 2016, at 1:21 PM, GitHub <sup...@github.com> wrote:

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] pygments vs. rouge in GitHub pages? font size control?
parts:
WSISYG is for losers!

It looks like the entries of an unordered list with more than one element
get wrapped in a <p> tag which yields the larger size, where as the single
element lists don’t get the same wrapping.

Maybe a bug in the SoSimple theme?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] pygments vs. rouge in GitHub pages? font size control?
parts:
OK --- hacking in a <p> doesn't work, because then the * doesn't get picked
up. So I went with <big> in the items themselves; that'll then have to be
removed if we change later.

Or someone with more patience than me might fix the format and markdown
processor (which Mitzi says is something called cramdown).

> WSISYG?

Did you mean WYSIWYG? I agree. I also hate markdown for the
same damn reason. It all tries to be too clever a la Microsoft
Word.

- Bob
